title: Ike's Morning Digest
data_note: Built from publisher RSS metadata (titles + teaser text). `coverage_window_hours` is the default (40h); several feeds use a longer `rollingHours` (see `scripts/build-digest.mjs`) so rows align with what is still on each publisher’s listing pages. Commercial Observer keeps its retail category + hub supplement; TRD adds a New York–filtered global retail tag feed. PincusCo uses the live site feed only (`/category/retail/feed/` is stale). **CRE Daily** retail briefs come from `credaily.com/sectors/retail/feed/`. **WSJ** is the Dow Jones real-estate feed with lifestyle and opinion dropped. **The New York Times** keeps real-estate and property stories only. **Traded** is commercial deal briefs from its news listing. Open each link for the full article (subscriptions may apply in the browser).

section_overviews.commercial_observer:
Danny Meyer Signs Greenwich Village Lease for New Restaurant: Fresh off his plans to open an eatery at the former Hotel Bossert in Brooklyn Heights, Michelin -star chef Danny Meyer is turning a hungry eye back on Manhattan. Meyer’s Union Square Hospitality Group signed a 10-year, roughly 8,000-square-foot lease at 21 West Eighth Street in Greenwich Village.

Australian Fashion Brand Mode Mischief Inks Lease at SoHo’s 65 Spring Street: Australian fashion brand Mode Mischief has signed a 2,000-square-foot retail lease at 65 Spring Street in Manhattan’s SoHo, Commercial Observer has learned. The deal converts the spot where the apparel company has held a pop-up location since May into its permanent home for the next five years.

Bondi Sushi to Open at Rockefeller’s 1221 Avenue of the Americas: Ah, salmon skin roll . New York and Miami-based Japanese restaurant brand Bondi Sushi has leased 4,400 square feet at Rockefeller Group ’s 1221 Avenue of the Americas in Rockefeller Center , the property owner announced Monday.

Williamsburg Secures Highest Retail Asking Rent in Brooklyn in 2026: REBNY: Williamsburg remains the shopping capital of Brooklyn. A flurry of leases and rising rents have defined the area in 2026, according to the Real Estate Board of New York (REBNY) ’ s most recent Brooklyn retail report, shared exclusively with Commercial Observer.
section_overviews.cre_daily:
JLL: Retail Vacancy Dips to 4.3% as Openings Beat Closures: U.S. retail net absorption totaled 8.3M SF in Q3 after 10.2M in Q2, and vacancy slipped to 4.3%.

Retail Investors Eye 2027 With Tight Supply, Rising Cap Rates: Retail investors enter 2027 weighing whether sellers’ pricing will match institutional targets, with cap rates expected to climb gradually and volume landing slightly below 2026 levels.

First Washington’s Alex Nyhan on Grocery-Anchored Retail: Guest: Alex Nyhan, CEO, First Washington Realty Alex Nyhan is CEO of First Washington Realty, one of the largest owners and operators of grocery-anchored and neighborhood retail in the country, with nearly 150 shopping centers across 22 states.

Simon Property Raises 2026 FFO Guidance After 4.7% Q3 Gain: Real Estate FFO rose 4.7% to $1.277 billion, or $3.37 per share, in Q3, and Simon lifted full-year guidance to $13.30 to $13.40 per share, up $0.10. Occupancy reached 96.5% in U.S.
section_overviews.new_york_post:
Ken Griffin sells NYC duplex to Jets owner for $58M — months after Mamdani’s pied-à-terre tax stunt: Hedge fund billionaire Ken Griffin has sold a sprawling Park Avenue duplex to New York Jets owner Woody Johnson for $58 million -- just months after Mayor Zohran Mamdani targeted the Citadel founder in a creepy video touting the lefty's new pied-à-terre tax.

Charming $10.5M NYC rooftop farmhouse finds a new owner just 1 month after listing for sale: This eye-catching Manhattan penthouse at 719 Greenwich St. is about to become someone's home, home on the range.

Gary Barnett’s Extell on development rampage in Manhattan: Although Barnett has his critics among competitors who call his strategy “ruthless,” no developer can boast of so many Manhattan projects as diverse as Extell’s.

Famed gallerist’s loft in NYC ‘It’ building asks $6M — a home previously owned by Calvin Klein: The sprawling two- to three-bedroom Police Building aerie is a combo of two separate units joined together by the fashion designer Klein.

items.headline: Danny Meyer Signs Greenwich Village Lease for New Restaurant
items.summary: Fresh off his plans to open an eatery at the former Hotel Bossert in Brooklyn Heights, Michelin -star chef Danny Meyer is turning a hungry eye back on Manhattan. Meyer’s Union Square Hospitality Group signed a 10-year, roughly 8,000-square-foot lease at 21 West Eighth Street in Greenwich Village. The property is owned by Grace Jean , tenant broker TSCG — formerly known as The Shopping Center Group — confirmed. The deal was signed Oct. 15.…

items.headline: Australian Fashion Brand Mode Mischief Inks Lease at SoHo’s 65 Spring Street
items.summary: Australian fashion brand Mode Mischief has signed a 2,000-square-foot retail lease at 65 Spring Street in Manhattan’s SoHo, Commercial Observer has learned. The deal converts the spot where the apparel company has held a pop-up location since May into its permanent home for the next five years. The asking rent was $575 per square foot, a source close to the deal told CO. Current Real Estate Advisors ’ Oded Nachmani represented the brand in this deal, which takes effect in January.…

items.headline: Bondi Sushi to Open at Rockefeller’s 1221 Avenue of the Americas
items.summary: Ah, salmon skin roll . New York and Miami-based Japanese restaurant brand Bondi Sushi has leased 4,400 square feet at Rockefeller Group ’s 1221 Avenue of the Americas in Rockefeller Center , the property owner announced Monday. The length of the lease and the asking rent were not disclosed. The average asking rent for retail space in Manhattan’s nearby Plaza District along Fifth Avenue between 49th and 59th streets was $2,471 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026, according to CBRE data.…

items.headline: JLL: Retail Vacancy Dips to 4.3% as Openings Beat Closures
items.summary: U.S. retail net absorption totaled 8.3M SF in Q3 after 10.2M in Q2, and vacancy slipped to 4.3%. Over 12 months the market absorbed 24.4M SF, versus a 7.0M SF loss a year earlier. Discount, off-price, grocery, fitness and entertainment tenants are backfilling boxes left by the 2024-2025 bankruptcy wave, often at higher rents. Net new supply is only 0.25% of inventory. Asking rents are up 1.8% against 3.7% inflation.…

items.headline: Retail Investors Eye 2027 With Tight Supply, Rising Cap Rates
items.summary: Retail investors enter 2027 weighing whether sellers’ pricing will match institutional targets, with cap rates expected to climb gradually and volume landing slightly below 2026 levels. Tenant demand for second-generation space stays active because high construction costs hold back new projects, and national retail vacancy sits near record lows.…

items.headline: Williamsburg Secures Highest Retail Asking Rent in Brooklyn in 2026: REBNY
items.summary: Williamsburg remains the shopping capital of Brooklyn. A flurry of leases and rising rents have defined the area in 2026, according to the Real Estate Board of New York (REBNY) ’ s most recent Brooklyn retail report, shared exclusively with Commercial Observer. In its report, REBNY tracked 16 retail corridors across Brooklyn from the fourth quarter of 2025 through the third quarter of 2026.…

items.headline: First Washington’s Alex Nyhan on Grocery-Anchored Retail
items.summary: Guest: Alex Nyhan, CEO, First Washington Realty Alex Nyhan is CEO of First Washington Realty, one of the largest owners and operators of grocery-anchored and neighborhood retail in the country, with nearly 150 shopping centers across 22 states. He joined the company in 2014 after stints as a special assistant in the mayor’s office in Washington, DC, and at Forest City Enterprises, where he worked on a 42-acre waterfront redevelopment on the Anacostia River.…

items.headline: Simon Property Raises 2026 FFO Guidance After 4.7% Q3 Gain
items.summary: Real Estate FFO rose 4.7% to $1.277 billion, or $3.37 per share, in Q3, and Simon lifted full-year guidance to $13.30 to $13.40 per share, up $0.10. Occupancy reached 96.5% in U.S. malls and Premium Outlets, base minimum rent rose 6.1% to $62.75 per SF, and reported retailer sales climbed 14.8% to $852 per SF. Net income fell to $1.54 per share from $1.86 on $99.6 million of non-cash losses, while the dividend rose 4.5% to $2.30 and Simon repurchased $236.5 million of its stock.…

items.headline: Car Wash Cap Rates Fall as Bonus Depreciation Lifts Demand
items.summary: Global Net Lease has 15 gas station, convenience and car wash properties under contract for about $70M at a 6.5% cash cap rate, versus 7.7% for other occupied sales this year. Gas station and car wash buildings count as 15-year property, so 100% bonus depreciation can cover the whole building without much cost segregation work. The Boulder Group put average single-tenant net lease asking cap rates at 6.92% in Q3, up 10 bps, while GNL sold office at a 7.5% cash cap rate.…

items.headline: Law Firm MoloLamken Relocates to 25K SF at RXR’s 590 Madison Avenue
items.summary: Law firm MoloLamken is relocating its Midtown Manhattan offices to RXR ’s 590 Madison Avenue , Commercial Observer has learned. The boutique law firm, which specializes in complex litigation, struck a deal for 24,839 square feet across the entire 16th floor of the office tower, according to an RXR spokesperson. MoloLamken’s moving day should be a breeze – the firm’s new space sits just one block west of its current office at 430 Park Avenue . The firm’s new lease carries a 10-year term.…

items.headline: Fashion Company Bestseller Renews 7K-SF Office, Showroom at 96 Spring Street
items.summary: Danish fashion company Bestseller has inked a lease renewal for its 7,400-square-foot corporate office and wholesale showroom in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. The 10-year agreement encompasses the company’s fourth-floor space at Midwood Investment ’s 96 Spring Street , according to a source familiar with the deal.…

items.headline: Mason Tenders’ District Council Trust Funds Extends 40K-SF Lease at 520 Eighth Avenue
items.summary: The administrative offices of Mason Tenders’ District Council Trust Funds plan to remain in Manhattan’s Penn District for at least another decade. The labor union fund, which provides employee benefits to active and retired workers in the construction industry, secured a 10-year extension deal at GFP Real Estate ’s 520 Eighth Avenue , according to a spokesperson for the landlord. The tenant will continue occupying 40,000 square feet of office space at the 26-story tower.…

items.headline: Fifth Avenue Retail Rents Jump 35% to Top Global Rankings
items.summary: Upper Fifth Avenue retail rents rose 35% year over year to an average of $2,700 a square foot, the highest in the world, per Cushman & Wakefield. Availability on upper Fifth dropped 4.4 percentage points to 13% in Q3, and brands such as Meta, Prada and Kering have made big commitments. The rebound mirrors a wider Manhattan recovery in office rents and hotel rates, and demand has spread to lower Fifth Avenue.…

items.headline: Sports Clothing Brand RBX Direct Signs 5K-SF Garment District Lease
items.summary: An activewear brand has signed a lease for an office and showroom in Manhattan’s Garment District. RBX Direct took 4,800 square feet at Lal Sani ’s 102 West 38th Street , where asking rent was $35 per square foot, according to landlord broker Adams & Company . Adams & Company did not disclose the length of the lease or the name of the landlord, but the most recent filings in property records show the building has not traded hands since 1994 when it was purchased by Sani.…

items.headline: Curbline Properties Seals $889M of Convenience Retail Acquisitions in 2026
items.summary: The nation’s largest owner of convenience retail is on an acquisitions binge, and doesn’t appear to be slowing down as 2026 comes to a close. Curbline Properties , a publicly traded real estate investment trust (REIT) with a 6 million-square-foot portfolio of unanchored convenience real estate, announced this week that it has acquired 82 convenience shopping centers this year for $888.9 million, and that it has already acquired 15 assets for $138.5 million so far in the fourth quarter, with more on the way.…

items.headline: Aaru Signs 27K-SF Sublease in Union Square With Plans for 650 NYC Employees
items.summary: A rapidly expanding artificial intelligence platform known for having “ rage rooms ” in its offices and other perks has signed a new lease near Manhattan’s Union Square . Aaru , founded only about two years ago, has signed a deal for 27,238 square feet to facilitate a five-year expansion plan from a headcount of 60 to about 650 employees in New York City at ZG Capital Partners ’ 836–838 Broadway , according to an announcement from Gov. Kathy Hochul . Aaru currently has offices at 199 Lafayette Street in Tribeca.…

items.headline: Japanese Pub Chain Shin Jidai Picks 26 St. Marks Place for First U.S. Location
items.summary: Shin Jidai , a Japanese casual pub brand, is coming stateside, and it’s selected Manhattan’s East Village for its first stop. The chain, through Shijidai Izakaya Group , has secured a 10-year lease at 26 St. Marks Place , according to a Tuesday announcement from tenant broker Lee & Associates NYC . Shin Jidai, founded in 2010, currently operates approximately 200 casual pubs, known as izakayas, across Japan.…

items.headline: Sui Yoga to Open 13K-SF Studio at 71 Fifth Avenue
items.summary: Wellness and fitness operator Sui Yoga has selected 71 Fifth Avenue for its second Manhattan location. The hot yoga, Pilates and strength training studio inked a 13-year deal for 13,000 square feet at the Midtown South building, located one block west of Union Square at the corner of Fifth Avenue and East 15th Street. Asking rent was $1.7 million per year. The deal involved the property’s previous landlord, Madison Capital , as well as its new owner.…
